title: MMC-Net: Mamba-based multi-level class-aware network for panchromatic and multispectral fusion classification
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Recent advances in remote sensing (RS) have improved panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) data acquisition, but challenges remain in multi-source fusion classification due to limitations in non-redundant feature extraction (i.e., effectively preserving complementary information while suppressing source-specific redundancies) and cross-source alignment (i.e., accurately matching spatial–spectral correspondences between PAN and MS data). The emerging state space model (SSM)-based Mamba model, with its global modeling and linear complexity, shows potential for complex land cover classification tasks. To this end, we propose MMC-Net, a novel Mamba-based multi-level class-aware network for PAN and MS fusion classification, which integrates a progressive fusion feature learning (PFFL) module and a multi-branch class-aware classification (MBCAC) module. The PFFL module employs dual-path spatial–spectral Mamba (S 2 Mamba) to extract discriminative features while suppressing redundancy through the feature reconstruction module (FRM), along with fusion Mamba (FMamba) to enable cross-source interaction via channel exchange and Fusion SSM. The MBCAC module enhances classification diversity through spatial-wise softmax and multi-branch learning, while its parameter-sharing mechanism across levels captures hierarchical discriminative patterns. Validated on three PAN-MS and one HSI-LiDAR datasets, MMC-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates robust, source-agnostic generalization across heterogeneous modalities. The code is available at https://github.com/Xidian-AIGroup190726/MMCNet .

title: Inst-Inpaint: Instructing to Remove Objects with Diffusion Models
abstract: Abstract Image inpainting task refers to erasing unwanted pixels from images and filling them in a semantically consistent and realistic way. Traditionally, the pixels that are wished to be erased are defined with binary masks. From the application point of view, a user needs to generate the masks for the objects they would like to remove which can be time-consuming and prone to errors. In this work, we are interested in an image inpainting algorithm that estimates which object to be removed based on natural language input and removes it, simultaneously. For this purpose, first, we construct a dataset named GQA-Inpaint for this task. Second, we present an inpainting framework, Inst-Inpaint , that can remove objects from images based on the instructions given as text prompts. We set various GAN and diffusion-based baselines and run experiments on synthetic and real-world image datasets. We compare methods with different evaluation metrics that measure the quality and accuracy of the models and show significant quantitative and qualitative improvements. Please refer to the web page of the project for the released code and dataset: http://instinpaint.abyildirim.com/

title: TokLIP: Marry Visual Tokens to CLIP for Multimodal Comprehension and Generation
abstract: Abstract Pioneering token-based works such as Chameleon and Emu3 have established a foundation for multimodal unification but face challenges of high training computational overhead and limited comprehension performance due to a lack of high-level semantics. In this paper, we introduce TokLIP, a visual tokenizer that enhances comprehension by semanticizing vector-quantized (VQ) tokens and incorporating CLIP-level semantics while enabling end-to-end multimodal autoregressive training with standard VQ tokens. TokLIP integrates a low-level discrete VQ tokenizer with a ViT-based token encoder to capture high-level continuous semantics. Unlike previous approaches (e.g., VILA-U) that discretize high-level features, TokLIP disentangles training objectives for comprehension and generation, allowing the direct application of advanced VQ tokenizers without the need for tailored quantization operations. Our empirical results demonstrate that TokLIP achieves exceptional data efficiency, empowering visual tokens with high-level semantic understanding while enhancing low-level generative capacity, making it well-suited for autoregressive Transformers in both open-world comprehension and generation tasks. The code and models are available at https://github.com/TencentARC/TokLIP .

title: SuperSVG++: Semantic-Driven Layer-Wise Scalable Vector Graphics Synthesis with Semantic Layer Decomposition
AnchorSED: A Segmentation Enhanced Detection Framework Based on Sparse Anchor for Multi-View 3D Object Detection
abstract: Existing 3D detection methods typically exploit 2D image information through region-level feature extraction and auxiliary semantic supervision. However, these strategies do not explicitly establish a correspondence between 3D candidates and corresponding 2D instance-level representations, which limits the ability to handle objects with complex shapes or severe occlusions. To address this limitation, we propose an anchorbased framework that establishes an anchor-conditioned 2D-3D interaction for jointly exploiting 2D and 3D annotations. Specifically, each 3D anchor and its sampled points are projected onto multiple image planes to identify anchor-associated regions of interest (ROIs), from which view-specific instance segmentation masks are predicted. These 2D representations are subsequently mapped back to their corresponding 3D anchors and aggregated through geometry-aware cross-modal feature alignment. Our approach extends conventional sparse detectors by introducing three components: (1) multi-view ROIs prediction, which maps 3D anchors and sampled points onto multi-view image planes to predict regions of interest (ROIs); (2) multi-view instance segmentation, generating pixel-accurate masks corresponding to predicted ROIs; and (3) cross-modal feature alignment, which fuses geometrically consistent 2D segmentation features with their associated 3D anchors. Furthermore, to bridge the geometric discrepancy between 2D images and 3D objects, we distill multi-scale visual knowledge from a pretrained large-scale self-supervised vision model into our detector, enhancing geometric consistency. Evaluated on the nuScenes benchmark, our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining computational efficiency. The code and auxiliary supervision data are available at https://github.com/HuiAuto/AnchorSED.

title: PRINT: A semi-empirical canopy water removal approach for improving estimates of leaf nitrogen and grain protein contents in winter wheat
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate estimation of leaf nitrogen content (LNC) and grain protein content (GPC) in winter wheat is crucial for making fertilization recommendations and assessing grain quality. Previous methods primarily relied on chlorophyll (Chl)-sensitive vegetation indices from the visible and near-infrared domain, while shortwave-infrared spectral features linked to dry matter and nitrogen remain underutilized due to strong leaf water masking. Although existing water removal methods can mitigate the absorption effects of leaf water, the reliability of the resulting simulated dry-canopy reflectance spectra (SDR) is limited by inaccurate leaf mass per area (LMA) retrieval. This study aimed to develop a semi-empirical water removal approach by integrating PRior knowledge and INitialization of leaf water conTent and LMA (PRINT) to simulate SDR, with the objective of improving the estimation performance of LNC and GPC. To achieve this goal, a Random Forest-based hybrid retrieval model was developed to increase LMA retrieval accuracy. Meanwhile, a visible and shortwave-based nitrogen index (VSNI) by combining the visible (proxy of Chl) and shortwave-infrared features was proposed for improving estimation performance of LNC and GPC. Moreover, experimental datasets covering multiple growth stages and geographic sites were collected to improve sample representativeness. These datasets were utilized to improve the retrieval of LMA and evaluate the performance of LNC and GPC estimations. The results demonstrated that the PRINT significantly improved the estimation accuracy of LMA over two standard physically-based inversion models (RMSE: 6.23 g/m 2 vs 8.25 g/m 2 and 45.73 g/m 2 ). Compared with existing VI-based models, the VSNI-based models yielded substantial improvements in LNC (R 2 : 0.62 ∼ 0.65, RMSE = 0.42 ∼ 0.54%) across sites, and enhanced GPC estimation accuracy up to R 2 = 0.66 (RMSE = 0.70%) at the peak filling stage across two years at one site. The proposed methodology advances the spectroscopic understanding of shortwave-infrared responses to nitrogen-related agronomic biochemicals, and holds significant potential for future applications in large-scale growth monitoring of wheat systems using satellite imagery.

title: High-resolution mapping of urban wet-bulb temperature and its intra-urban variability: A London case study
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Most extreme-heat studies map high-resolution near-surface dry-bulb air temperature ( T a ), yet wet-bulb temperature ( T w ) fields that can capture the combined effects of T a and humidity to represent human heat stress remain limited. This data gap constrains investigation of intra-urban heat variability and the timing of peak heat stress. Here, based on the Rankine-Kirchhoff approximations of Romps, this study innovatively generates hourly 1-km T w by integrating crowdsourced station observations with remote sensing and reanalysis data in machine learning based downscaling frameworks. Taking London during the summers of 2019–2022 as a case study, the tuned RF-based downscaling approach achieved the best performance ( MAE = 0.65 °C, RMSE = 0.93 °C, R 2 = 0.91) among all models. The resulting T w patterns diverge from those commonly reported for T a : blue infrastructure shows no consistent cooling effect, whereas vegetated areas cool T w increasingly as tree cover rises, pointing to tree-dominated green infrastructure as a promising humid-heat countermeasure. Results further show that daily maximum T w occurs 0.7 h earlier than daily maximum T a in London, opposite to findings elsewhere, implying that climate type and coastal influence modulate the timing of peak T w , which may affect the attribution of excess nighttime mortality. Besides, a systematic global assessment of the mechanisms controlling T w extremes is also required in the future.

title: Eyegent: Visual Attention Orchestration on Concepts
abstract: Abstract Where a human looks is not random, nor is it merely a reflex to visual salience. It is a decision shaped by goals, constrained by language, and driven by the need to resolve uncertainty. We propose Eyegent , an active vision agent built on this premise: that visual search is best understood as sequential Bayesian inference over semantically grounded hypotheses, with fixations serving as epistemic actions. Given an image and a natural-language query, Eyegent constructs a discrete hypothesis space of candidate segmentation masks, maintains an explicit posterior belief distribution, and selects each fixation to maximise expected information gain—updating beliefs via vision–language model verification and terminating when uncertainty falls below a principled risk threshold. We formalise this process as Bayesian Active Semantic Grounding (BASG), a computational-level account that provides formal guarantees on belief concentration, entropy reduction, and bounded decision risk. The framework is neurobiologically grounded in the large-scale network organisation of the human brain, with the Salience Network identified as the dynamic orchestrator of semantic, inferential, and oculomotor processes. Critically, Eyegent requires no gaze supervision and no task-specific training: it is zero-shot, modular, and built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Evaluated on RefCOCO-Gaze and AiR-D, two benchmarks coupling language-driven visual tasks with human eye-tracking ground truth, Eyegent achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance among zero-shot methods across semantic, spatial, and structural scanpath metrics, and approaches supervised baselines on several dimensions. The result is a system that does not merely predict where humans look, but generates scanpaths for the same reason humans generate them: to find out.

title: $${\text {VLScene}}^{++}$$: Enhancing 3D Semantic Scene Completion via VLM Discrepancy-Aware Semantic Distillation and Sparse–Dense Hybrid Awareness
Smart transfer: Leveraging vision foundation model for rapid building damage mapping with post-earthquake VHR imagery
Continental-scale Sentinel-1 InSAR deformation rate mosaics of central North America
abstract: Ground deformation driven by natural and anthropogenic processes poses significant risks to infrastructure and public safety. Although many regions have been studied, large areas remain poorly characterized because they are remote, sparsely populated, or not expected to experience deformation. Nevertheless, unrecognized natural and anthropogenic processes can produce substantial ground deformation. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides high-resolution, high-precision measurements and enables systematic, cost-effective monitoring over large areas. Here, we present continental-scale ground deformation rate mosaics over central North America, covering the contiguous United States together with adjacent parts of southern Canada and northern Mexico, derived from over 77,000 Sentinel-1 SAR images acquired between 2014 and 2026. The dataset includes both ascending and descending acquisitions, organized into 522 frames and processed using a fully automated workflow and the Multidimensional Small Baseline Subset (MSBAS) software for time-series analysis. Atmospheric phase delays were corrected using a power-law model that also removed long-wavelength signals ( > 20 km), which improved the precision of the remaining short-wavelength signals and placed the resulting rates in a distributed local reference frame. Four mosaics were generated: ascending and descending line-of-sight, and horizontal east-west and vertical deformation components, with corresponding standard error estimates. The high-pass-filtered mosaics, produced at 40 m spatial resolution, reveal spatially coherent deformation patterns, with mean standard errors between 8.9 and 12.6 mm/yr. Temporal coverage is spatially nonuniform, and some signals may reflect processes other than ground deformation. Nonetheless, these products are valuable for identifying new areas of potential concern and guiding site-specific investigations. Several illustrative examples are provided to demonstrate the broad range of detected signals. All datasets are publicly available on Mendeley Data and are expected to support scientific research and regulatory applications.

title: Enhancing soil property retrieval in an Ali-Perudic Argosols–dominated region through multi-angle hyperspectral feature integration
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Soil bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) is strongly influenced by soil physicochemical properties, yet most hyperspectral retrieval studies rely on single-view reflectance, leaving the value of multi-angle information insufficiently explored. In this study, bidirectional reflectance factors (BRFs) were measured at 48 viewing angles for 156 soil samples collected from a region dominated by Ali-Perudic Argosols. An optimal multi-angle retrieval framework was developed for different soil properties by systematically comparing spectral preprocessing methods, feature extraction, and modeling algorithms. The effects of viewing angle on retrieval accuracy and feature wavelength distribution were further analyzed, and the applicability of simulated multi-angle BRFs generated using SOILSPECT model was further assessed. Results show that the optimal framework for single-view reflectance combines Savitzky–Golay (SG) smoothing, a hybrid random frog–competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (RFROG–CARS) feature selection strategy, and nonlinear support vector machine (SVM) regression. Retrieval accuracy varied substantially with viewing geometry, and no universal optimal viewing angle was identified across soil properties. For multi-angle BRF data, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) feature extraction approach outperformed the RFROG–CARS wavelength selection method. Specifically, R 2 (RMSE) improved from 0.64 (8.8 g/kg) to 0.73 (7.7 g/kg) for SOM content, from 0.53 (6.9 %) to 0.61 (6.3 %) for sand content, and from 0.64 (4.7 %) to 0.69 (4.4 %) for silt content, while remaining comparable for cation exchange capacity (0.77/2.4 cmol/kg to 0.76/2.4 cmol/kg) and clay content (0.80/4.3 % to 0.79/4.3 %). Although the retrieval accuracy based on multi-angle BRFs remained slightly lower than that obtained from the optimal viewing geometry, it consistently outperformed most individual viewing angles. The selected multi-angle hyperspectral features were distributed across nearly all viewing angles, indicating complementary spectral–geometric information. Although retrieval accuracy based on simulated BRFs was lower than that based on measured BRFs, the results were broadly comparable. These findings support the use of multi-angle information in soil spectroscopy and remote sensing applications.

title: A physics-constrained superpixel-based multi-source remote sensing spatiotemporal fusion network
abstract: Remote sensing spatiotemporal fusion aims to generate image sequences with both high spatial and temporal resolution. However, many deep learning approaches treat fusion as a black-box regression problem, overlooking differences in sensor imaging physics—such as the point spread function (PSF) and pixel-area integration—which often leads to boundary blurring, spectral mixing, or even physically implausible high-frequency details over heterogeneous landscapes. In addition, these methods commonly rely on paired coarse-/fine-resolution reference images at the same time, which limits data availability. To address these issues, we propose SPP-STF, a superpixel-based fusion network trained with a physics-guided degradation-consistency regularizer that requires only a reference fine-resolution image and a target coarse-resolution observation, while deriving an edge intensity map as a structural prior. The model adopts a U-Net-style, three-branch encoder–decoder to fuse texture, temporal variation, and edge cues at multiple scales. An EdgeResBlock uses high-frequency gating to sharpen boundaries and reduce cross-class leakage, and a superpixel cross-attention Transformer learns object-level correspondences to alleviate alignment errors caused by mixed pixels. During training, we introduce a learnable anisotropic Gaussian PSF-based degradation-consistency term: the predicted fine-resolution output is blurred and downsampled via area integration to match the observed coarse image, and this term is optimized jointly with the reconstruction loss. Quantitatively, SPP-STF achieves the best RMSE, SAM, PSNR, and UIQI on CIA (0.0254, 0.1522, 31.9330 dB, and 0.8451), the best results across all six metrics on LGC (including RMSE 0.0188 and PSNR 34.6307 dB), and the best RMSE, SSIM, SAM, PSNR, and ERGAS on Tianjin (0.0410, 0.7640, 0.2459, 27.8666 dB, and 30.4838). Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of the superpixel and edge modules. The PSF term is interpreted here as a training-time regularizer that provides consistent and physically more reasonable improvements across the three datasets. Structured pruning further indicates that the model can retain spatial structure under substantial compression, while spectral fidelity becomes notably more sensitive beyond roughly 70% pruning.

title: BCP3D: Robust 3D Object Tracking Using Brain-Inspired Complementary-Pathway for Challenging Scenarios

Robust reinforcement learning multi-baseline phase unwrapping algorithm with JPEG-LS
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Multi-baseline (MB) phase unwrapping (PU) breaks through the limitations of the phase continuity assumption, but existing MBPU algorithms cannot adapt well to noisy environments. A robust reinforcement learning integer programming multi-baseline PU algorithm with JPEG-LS (RL-MBPU) is proposed. First, the cutting plane–pure integer programming cut-selection process is formulated as a sequential reinforcement-learning problem. An efficacy-guided imitation strategy is used to initialize an MBPU-structure-aware single-cut policy, which is further optimized by an actor–critic method using Cut-PAR2-based trajectory returns to reduce the root-node proof cost. Finally, the initial ambiguity number solution is corrected using dynamic median edge detector based on JPEG-LS, and the PU is completed by using the prediction of the left, top, and top-left neighbors of the current pixel and combining it with the local gradient threshold determination. In both simulation and real data experiments, the RL-MBPU algorithm demonstrated stable PU performance, including computational efficiency and noise robustness for interferograms of different sizes. Compared with the minimum-cost flow and cutting plane–pure integer programming algorithms, the RL-MBPU algorithm reduces the root mean square error by approximately 61.2% and 14.5%, respectively, while improving efficiency by approximately 54.1% and 42.4%, respectively. This can further support high-precision interferometric synthetic aperture radar applications.

title: Airborne observatory for high-resolution land surface temperature and spectral emissivity
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The Land surface temperature and emissivity Airborne Observatory System (LAOS) provides land surface temperature (LST) and spectral land surface emissivity (LSE) at very high spatial resolutions (0.5–4 m) and flexible (e.g., intraday) acquisition times. LAOS enables: (i) to map spectral variations in LSE—an inherent property of land surface materials—and (ii) to analyse spatial and temporal variations in LST in relation to land surface processes. Here, we present the scientific rationale for developing the system, the components of the hardware and the processing chain, and retrieval and validation results from an agricultural case study. The LAOS hardware consists of a HyperCam-LW (Telops Inc.), a Fourier transformed infrared spectrometer that operates in the long-wave infrared (7.7–11.5 µm) and an associated airborne platform. The processing chain includes radiometric calibration, generation of ortho -photo mosaics, noise removal, atmospheric correction (AC) and temperature and emissivity separation (TES). Key innovations with respect to previous airborne hyperspectral TIR studies are an improved noise filtering step and a recalibrated minimum emissivity—spectral contrast relationship derived from an extended set of ECOSTRESS spectral library spectra . For demonstrating LAOS’ capacities, an extensive survey campaign was conducted over the Burana Irrigation Consortium area near Modena, Italy, on 13–15 July 2022. Images were acquired at 1- and 4-meter resolution during three times of the day. Raw image tiles were processed to LST and LSE mosaics and compared with ground measurements. Validation was performed over agricultural surfaces – wheat stubble, melon, and water –providing a more surface-type-diverse assessment than previous more urban-focused studies. The LST mosaics show good agreement with the in-situ temperatures across all three surface types (within-class R 2 = 0.52–0.86, RMSE = 2.0–3.2 K, global R 2 = 0.96). LSE maps reveal crisp changes at field boundaries and appear relatively constant over time (i.e., both during a day and across multiple days). Airborne LSE spectra show mostly reasonable agreement with ground measurements and reproduce the overall spectral shape. Spectral emissivity remains largely stable both diurnally and across days (average variability ∼ 1.1 %), indicating consistent retrieval performance at field scale. The results demonstrate that LAOS produces LST and LSE maps with accuracies consistent with previous hyperspectral TIR studies, showcasing its potential to address pressing questions in various fields, including agriculture (e.g., irrigation), forestry (e.g., stress detection), defence (e.g., target detection), and urban studies (e.g., urban heat islands). As a high spatial resolution airborne TIR imager, LAOS can also serve as a demonstrator for upcoming satellite missions, such as LSTM (Land Surface Temperature Monitoring, ESA), TRISHNA (Thermal Infrared Satellite for High-Resolution Applications, CNES & ISRO), and Eagle-TIR (Explorer for Artemis Geology Lunar and Earth, NASA).

title: Multi-evidence-based assessment and selection of nine reconstructed solar-induced fluorescence products over China
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The availability of multiple long-term reconstructed solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) datasets at varying spatiotemporal resolutions provides new opportunities for investigating vegetation dynamics, particularly for estimating gross primary productivity (GPP) and assessing ecosystem responses to environmental stress. Evaluating the consistency and performance of reconstructed SIF (SIFr) products across different land cover types is therefore essential for their effective application in carbon–water cycle studies. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of nine widely used SIFr products (GOSIF, CSIF, RTSIF, LTSIF, HSIF, JJSIF, PKSIF, DSIF, and HCSIF) across China at a spatial resolution of 0.05° and a monthly temporal scale over the period 2007–2016. A multi-source validation framework was employed, integrating tower-based SIF, site-level and gridded GPP, and the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index. We found that although all SIFr products exhibited strong agreement in long-term spatial patterns, substantial discrepancies existed in interannual trends. Agreement in long-term mean spatial patterns was generally higher than that in the spatial patterns of temporal trends and varied across land cover types, with stronger agreement observed in grasslands and croplands and lower agreement in forests. Across multiple validation datasets, RTSIF shows comparatively favorable performance, followed by CSIF and GOSIF, which exhibit similar performance. CSIF performs relatively well for GPP but shows lower performance in representing meteorological moisture conditions. Furthermore, product performance exhibits clear land cover dependence, with more reliable results in structurally simple ecosystems and reduced performance in complex canopy environments. We also identified differences in the relative performance of SIFr products across application scenarios and land cover types. These findings highlight the importance of product selection tailored to research objectives and environmental conditions and provide useful information for SIF-based monitoring of vegetation dynamics.

title: Global offshore wind development (2015–2025): multiscale structural evolution based on object-level sar mapping
abstract: Offshore wind is an important renewable infrastructure supporting the global energy transition, making accurate offshore wind turbine (OWT) mapping essential for understanding infrastructure expansion and informing marine spatial management. Existing long-term approaches often extend single-period detections over time based on structural-stability assumptions, but accumulated identification errors and regional imaging differences limit consistent object-level representation across years and regions. To address this challenge, this study proposes a coordinated three-stage object-level SAR mapping framework, in which a stable and balanced sample representation strategy under unified annual temporal windows provides a consistent data basis across regions and years. On this basis, the lightweight YOLO-SAR model integrates frequency-aware feature modeling and hierarchical structural representation to improve OWT detection under heterogeneous conditions. Compared with YOLO11n, YOLO-SAR reduces the parameter count from 2.58 M to 2.30 M while improving mAP@0.5:0.95 from 0.3956 to 0.4553. Spatial reconstruction then transforms detection outputs into consistent annual object-level OWT maps, forming a continuous spatial database covering 2015–2025. Multi-region validation and comparisons with public datasets further support the reliability of these spatial records. These records reveal multiscale patterns of offshore wind spatial evolution: shifts in regional contributions reshape global growth, regional expansion pathways and internal spatial restructuring exhibit stage-dependent differences, and site-boundary expansion and turbine-spacing adjustments determine local spatial organization. These findings demonstrate that global offshore wind development is not merely a process of quantitative growth, but a multiscale spatial evolution driven by regional shifts, site expansion, and internal spatial reorganization. The proposed framework provides a consistent data foundation for global offshore wind evolution analysis and can be extended to other marine energy infrastructures.

title: LexSign: Learning Sign Language from Lexical Descriptions
Zero-Shot Domain Generalization via Domain Prompt Learning
PASG-RoboKeyBench: A Closed-Loop Automated Framework and Benchmark for Operation Primitive Extraction and Semantic Anchoring in Robotic Manipulation
30-meter land surface temperature from Landsat via progressive self-training downscaling
Quantifying anisotropic impacts of LCZ landscape patterns on NO2 variabilities in the Yangtze River Delta, China
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Urban landscape patterns strongly affect air quality, yet existing studies often neglect anisotropic processes, rely on arbitrary fixed-radius buffers, and lack standardized classification frameworks. To overcome these limitations, we developed a novel analytical framework that integrates high-accuracy Local Climate Zone (LCZ) classification, multi-scale spatial modeling, and a shape-adaptive influence zone. Central to this framework is the Adaptive Directionally Weighted Sector Influence Zone (ADWSIZ), a new method that explicitly captures the directional heterogeneity of landscape effects on pollutants. Applied to station-based NO 2 measurements in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) urban agglomeration, we used multi-scale Geographically Weighted Ridge Regression (GWRR) to identify a 4000 m circular buffer as the optimal modeling scale, revealing a clear decoupling from the intrinsic static LCZ pattern scale (approximately 1000 m). Building upon this optimal distance, the ADWSIZ model was developed to refine the influence zone’s shape. The application of ADWSIZ improved model performance (Adjusted R 2 : 0.464 → 0.506 ; RMSE: 2.950 → 2.834 µg/m 3 ) and reduced residual spatial autocorrelation. Our findings highlight that the anisotropic influence of features like industrial land and compact high-rise fabrics is a critical, previously underexplored factor in explaining NO 2 variation. This study establishes a replicable and transferable methodology that advances the conceptualization of influence zones from simple distance-based buffers to scale- and shape-adaptive forms, offering a robust tool for refining spatial coupling analyses between urban morphology and air pollutants.

title: An interpretable DM-PINN for retrieving mangrove canopy carbon, nitrogen, and potassium contents using Sentinel-2 and SDGSAT-1 observations along China's southeastern coast
abstract: Mangroves are among the most important blue carbon ecosystems, contributing substantially to global carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Canopy carbon (CCC), nitrogen (CNC), and potassium (CKC) contents provide critical indicators of nutrient cycling, ecosystem functioning, and ecological health. However, the structural complexity and strong spatial heterogeneity of mangroves present major obstacles to understanding the spectral response mechanisms and achieving reliable large-scale retrieval of these biochemical parameters. To address these limitations, we developed an interpretable retrieval framework that integrates causal analysis with physical constraints for reliable estimation of mangrove biochemical parameters. First, we proposed a Multi-Channel Chatterjee-Enhanced Correlation Spectrum Analysis (MC-ξ-CS) method that integrates causal discovery to systematically identify spectral bands causally associated with CCC, CNC, and CKC. For large-scale retrieval of mangrove canopy parameters, the identified causal relationships were transferred to satellite observations through a Global Angle-Divergence Spectral Transfer (GADT) framework, yielding robust estimation (R2 = 0.511–0.669). Subsequently, a Dual-Mechanism Guided Physics-Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) was developed to synergistically integrate causal analysis and physical constraints, achieving robust retrieval performance (R2 = 0.604–0.83) for three representative mangrove species and enhancing the physical interpretability of the results. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first comprehensive large-scale retrieval of key mangrove biochemical parameters along the southeastern coast of China, revealing CCC values of 409.18–566.89 g/kg (C/N = 9.77–14.21), CNC values of 14.38–74.9 g/kg (N/K = 1.99–3.86), and CKC values of 4.78–19.67 g/kg (C/K = 28.22–37.67). Distinct inter-provincial spatial patterns were observed: CNC and CKC exhibited similar gradients, increasing from landward to seaward regions, whereas CCC displayed an opposite spatial distribution pattern with lower values in coastal regions. Moreover, CCC was strongly positively correlated with CNC, while CKC showed negative correlations with both parameters. Collectively, this study established a novel theoretical and methodological framework for elucidating the spectral response mechanisms of mangrove biochemical parameters, offering critical scientific support for large-scale mangrove degradation monitoring, ecological restoration assessment, and biodiversity conservation.

title: Wavelet-guided decomposition of two-dimensional InSAR time series: insights into long-term settlement and cyclic deformation of a high earth-rockfill dam
abstract: Long-term deformation of high earth-rockfill dams reflects post-construction consolidation, creep, reservoir loading, and cyclic operation. Separating these superimposed components is essential for gaining process-level insights into spatial patterns and differential responses. This study investigates the Pubugou Dam, a 186 m high earth-rockfill dam in Southwest China, using ascending and descending Sentinel-1 observations from 2017–2023. The two viewing geometries were jointly inverted to recover vertical and east-west displacements. A wavelet-guided decomposition, in which dominant periods identified by the continuous wavelet transform constrain the window length and component grouping in singular spectrum analysis, was proposed to separate the displacement records into long-term trend, annual cyclic, and residual components. Synthetic experiments yielded root mean square errors of 0.69–2.16 mm, indicating effective decomposition performance. Cross wavelet transform and wavelet transform coherence quantified localized coherence and phase lags between the cyclic components and reservoir water level. The central earth-rockfill body exhibits the largest magnitudes of vertical and east-west deformation rates, whereas the spillway and abutments remained comparatively stable. The trend components and settlement indices are consistent with relatively slow long-term post-construction settlement during the observation period. Annual cyclic deformation is more pronounced in the east-west direction and exhibits spatially variable lags relative to reservoir level fluctuations. Settlement inclination and apparent horizontal strain remain low under the adopted criteria, suggesting limited crest-cracking susceptibility during the observation period. This work demonstrates how wavelet-guided decomposition of two-dimensional InSAR time series provides spatially explicit insights into long-term settlement and cyclic deformation of high earth-rockfill dams.

title: Learning Complex Scene Segmentation from Noisy Label
Dust aerosol properties and radiative effects over the global oceans from synergistic spaceborne observations and modeling
Reconstructing multi-temporal Glacier area changes to improve mass balance estimates in the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau (2000–2025)
abstract: The southeastern Tibetan Plateau (SETP), a critical component of the “Asian Water Tower”, hosts a large concentration of maritime temperate glaciers that are highly sensitive to climate change. However, persistent cloud cover, seasonal snow, and supraglacial debris complicate consistent long-term glacier mapping, while the use of static glacier boundaries may introduce temporal mismatches in altimetry-based glacier mass-change estimates. In this study, we developed a multi-source data-fusion framework on Google Earth Engine (GEE) to reconstruct glacier-area changes in the SETP from 2000 to 2025 at five-year intervals and 30 m spatial resolution. Random Forest classifiers were used to integrate Landsat and Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Sentinel-1 synthetic-aperture-radar data, and NASADEM-derived topographic information, supporting glacier delineation under complex surface and atmospheric conditions. The reconstructed glacier area decreased from 8,083 ± 664 km2 in 2000 to 6,228 ± 572 km2 in 2025, corresponding to a cumulative loss of 22.9 ± 3.6% and a mean loss rate of 80.51 ± 10.51 km2 yr−1. The mean area-loss rates were 51.31 ± 6.51 km2 yr−1 during 2000–2010 and 92.99 ± 15.55 km2 yr−1 during 2010–2025, indicating a higher average loss rate in the later period. By combining satellite-altimetry-derived elevation changes from ICESat, CryoSat-2, and ICESat-2 with the reconstructed time-varying glacier areas, we estimated a mean glacier mass-change rate of −6.51 ± 1.22 Gt yr−1 during 2003–2022. Compared with using a fixed 2003 glacier area, the time-varying-area calculation reduced the estimated mass-loss magnitude by 0.63 Gt yr−1, equivalent to 8.8% of the fixed-area estimate. These results indicate that incorporating time-varying glacier areas can reduce temporal mismatch in altimetry-based mass-change estimation and improve the temporal consistency of regional glacier mass-change assessments.

title: Test-Time Computing for Referring Multimodal Large Language Models
Event-Guided Decomposition from a Long-Exposure Nighttime Snapshot into Video Sequence
A CNN-based mapping approach for aeolian dunes in Arctic Sweden
Second-dimension-enhanced spatial context-aware modeling for spatial prediction
abstract: Spatial prediction is a fundamental task in geographic information science and environmental resource assessment. However, under complex terrain and heterogeneous covariates, models relying only on point-scale attributes or a single global relationship often have difficulty representing spatial context and regional heterogeneity. This study proposes a second-dimension-enhanced spatial context-aware modeling framework (SDA-SCA) that integrates first-dimension covariates, neighborhood-based second-dimension features, covariate screening, spatially constrained stratification, and local model training. Using two independently constructed annual spatial-prediction cases based on surface solar radiation observations from 670 stations in China in 2022 and 2023, five modeling schemes—Ordinary Kriging, Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF), first-dimension attribute modeling (FDA), second-dimension augmented modeling (SDA), and SDA-SCA—were evaluated under spatial cross-validation. SDA-SCA showed a consistent predictive advantage across the two independent annual cases and the three evaluated model families. Relative to FDA, SDA-SCA increased R2 by 0.11–0.16 in 2022 and 0.17–0.21 in 2023, while reducing RMSE by 12.4%–17.7% and 24.3%–33.7%, and MAE by 22.8%–35.5% and 31.5%–50.4%, respectively. Stage-wise ablation showed that the FDA-to-SDA step produced consistent but moderate improvements, whereas the SDA-to-SDA-SCA step provided larger and more stable gains. These results indicate that second-dimension features improve the representation of neighborhood context, and their predictive value is further strengthened when coupled with spatial stratification. SHAP analysis further confirmed the substantial contribution of second-dimension features to the integrated model. The proposed framework provides an extensible pathway for spatial prediction tasks requiring the joint representation of local attributes, neighborhood context, and spatial heterogeneity.

title: Transforming Leaf-Off LiDAR to leaf-on canopy height models using deep learning
abstract: Accurate tree canopy metrics are essential for a wide range of ecological, environmental, and climate studies. Recent advances in airborne LiDAR sensing have greatly expanded access to high-resolution three-dimensional observations of tree canopy structure. However, many widely available airborne LiDAR datasets are acquired under leaf-off conditions to support terrain mapping, and our analysis across ecologically diverse sites shows that canopy height models (CHMs) derived from these data exhibit substantial, recurring discrepancies in canopy height and extent, with an overall tendency to underrepresent canopy structure relative to leaf-on conditions. These discrepancies limit the direct use of leaf-off CHMs in applications requiring canopy information representative of leaf-on conditions. To address this limitation, we introduce a deep learning framework for reconstructing leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs. To our knowledge, this is the first study to formulate the direct reconstruction of leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs as a supervised image-to-image learning task. The framework provides two complementary models: a Pix2Pix model that uses the leaf-off CHM alone and a U-Net model that additionally incorporates multispectral imagery. Our proposed models achieve robust canopy-height accuracy across four spatially independent test sites (R²: 0.85–0.92; Mean Absolute Error: 1.3–1.6 metres), substantially reducing the discrepancies observed in the leaf-off source CHMs. They also provide sharper delineation of canopy details and higher accuracy than recent optical-imagery-based approaches. To facilitate broader use, we developed an open-access web application that deploys the pre-trained models and supports on-demand leaf-on CHM generation for user-selected areas across the U.S. where suitable leaf-off LiDAR inputs are available. Overall, the framework provides a practical means to bridge the seasonal data gap in LiDAR acquisition and improve access to reliable canopy metrics representative of leaf-on conditions.

title: Passive microwave sea ice concentration biases in the Southern Hemisphere revealed by ICESat-2 linear ice fraction
A revised model for atmospheric adjacency effect correction in optical satellite earth observation images
abstract: Adjacency effects, caused by atmospheric scattering, constitute a significant source of error in optical satellite surface reflectance retrievals, accounting for up to 50% of the measured signal near sharp reflectance contrasts. This study derives an improved analytical model for the atmospheric Point Spread Function (PSF) as a function of atmospheric and geometric parameters, using the GPU-accelerated SMART-G Monte Carlo model. Among four formulations compared, the two-parameter King kernel is the most suitable for lookup-table parameterisation across aerosol optical thickness (AOT), wavelength, aerosol species and vertical distribution, relative humidity, viewing geometry, and ground elevation. For artificial landscapes, the King model reduces the RMSE of surface reflectance retrieval by a factor of 3 to 11 compared to Wu et al., 2024, and by more than one order of magnitude compared to the widely used Gaussian model, at nadir and off-nadir angles up to 16 ∘ . Validation on Sentinel-2 scenes over Cairo and Arcachon Bay confirms relative TOA errors below 1% for the King model, while the Gaussian model systematically underestimates reflectance in high-contrast areas. Comparison with in-situ marine reflectances from the GLORIA dataset shows RMSE reductions of up to 57% over the Gaussian model and up to 11% over Wu et al., 2024 in the near-infrared. A sensitivity analysis shows that AOT is the dominant parameter, followed by wavelength, aerosol species and vertical distribution, while solar zenith angle has no influence for Lambertian surfaces and viewing zenith angle is negligible within the Sentinel-2 field of view.

title: Deep learning detection of submesoscale eddies from MODIS SST in the South China Sea
abstract: Submesoscale eddies play crucial roles in oceanic energy cascades and material transport; however, their detection faces substantial challenges owing to inadequate spatial resolution in traditional satellite altimetric measurements. This research introduces Sub-Eddy-Net, an innovative deep learning approach utilizing an enhanced YOLOv8-SGAM architecture for identifying submesoscale eddy features within MODIS-derived sea surface temperature (SST) imagery across the South China Sea region. By exploiting SST data's advantageous temporal coverage and observational continuity relative to altimetric sensors, synthetic aperture radar, and ocean color products, the developed algorithm demonstrates detection precision of 0.968, successfully identifying 20,443 submesoscale eddies throughout 2015–2024. Results indicate cyclonic eddy prevalence exceeds anticyclonic occurrences, exhibiting average radii of 13.1 km and 13.7 km respectively. Eddy distributions primarily cluster within coastal waters and Luzon Strait vicinity, displaying pronounced seasonal patterns. Comparison with Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) observations shows 64.3% matched features, 27.1% positional offsets, and 8.6% detected only in SST. Within the same eddies, coherent chlorophyll-a (Chla) signatures were present in a smaller fraction, indicating that SST is the more robust tracer for systematic detection. This Sub-Eddy-Net methodology offers a scalable approach for examining submesoscale oceanic phenomena, providing a decadal inventory for further study of their roles in ocean circulation and vertical exchange.

title: Integrating Landsat and ECOSTRESS to explore the value of additional thermal infrared satellite observations for field-scale evapotranspiration mapping
abstract: Landsat has provided an indispensable foundation for field-scale evapotranspiration (ET) mapping but is constrained by its overpass temporal frequency. Although integrating additional thermal data offers a pathway to bridge this gap, the magnitude of improvement varies across observation characteristics and surface context and remains less understood. Here, ECOsystem Spaceborne Thermal Radiometer Experiment on Space Station (ECOSTRESS) is used as an additional thermal source on top of the Landsat baseline to evaluate the value of more frequent thermal observations for improving field-scale ET time series. We implemented a Google Earth Engine -based Disaggregated Atmosphere-Land Exchange Inverse + Data Mining Sharpener framework to generate a Landsat-based ET baseline and enhanced it with ECOSTRESS observations. The resulting ET data was validated across 25 flux-tower sites spanning diverse land-cover types and climate zones across the contiguous United States. When integrated with Landsat, the addition of ECOSTRESS observations reduced interpolation errors and improved temporal consistency across most sites. However, improvements in ET time series agreement depended strongly on (1) the extent to which ECOSTRESS reduced effective Landsat sampling gaps and (2) the accuracy of overpass-day ECOSTRESS ET retrievals. Improvements were largest when ECOSTRESS shortened Landsat observation gaps by ~50% and maintained high scene quality. ECOSTRESS overpass time also influenced performance, with acquisitions between 10:00–14:00 producing most reliable ET estimates. These results support developing methods with multi-satellite observations to strengthen field-scale ET and help address the key knowledge gap regarding the value of increased thermal observations.

title: Twin-satellite constraints from GF-5B and DQ-1 enable hourly near-surface NO2 estimation across China
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a major air pollutant with significant impacts on human health, yet satellite-based estimates of surface NO 2 with full diurnal coverage remain limited. Here, we develop a machine learning framework to estimate hourly near-surface NO 2 concentrations across China by integrating complementary observations from two Chinese polar-orbiting satellites, GF-5B (~10:30 local time) and DQ-1 (~13:30 local time). A Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model driven by twin-satellite NO 2 vertical column densities (VCDs) and meteorological reanalysis achieves strong predictive performance in 10-fold cross-validation, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.91 and root mean square error (RMSE) of 5.40 μg/m 3 across all hours (4.46 μg/m 3 during daytime; 6.32 μg/m 3 at night), and retains reasonable skill under stricter site-based, time-based, and independent cross-year validation. The reconstructed dataset captures the characteristic diurnal cycle of NO 2 , with morning and evening peaks associated with traffic emissions and a midday minimum driven by photochemical loss. Compared to the single-satellite TROPOMI product, the twin-satellite configuration substantially improves the representation of diurnal variability, increasing R 2 from 0.81 to 0.91 and reducing RMSE by 31.60%, and corrects a distorted urban-rural NO 2 exposure ratio (1.70 for TROPOMI versus a ground-based 1.19), narrowing it to 1.30. Feature-importance analysis further shows that meteorological variables dominate model predictions during both day and night, with satellite VCDs providing a complementary, though indirect, constraint on nighttime concentrations. The resulting hourly NO 2 dataset demonstrates the value of synergistic multi-satellite observations for air quality monitoring and provides a robust basis for refined pollution control and population exposure assessment.

title: A GeoAI framework for remote-sensing-driven traffic activity and emission intensity in a data-scarce megacity
abstract: In rapidly expanding megacities across the Global South, a profound data scarcity paradox frequently prevents effective environmental monitoring and evidence driven urban planning. While severe traffic congestion generates acute localised pollution, the total absence of continuous municipal traffic counters, ubiquitous vehicle telemetry, and air quality monitoring networks leaves these environments empirically unmonitored. This study resolves this challenge by introducing a reproducible geocomputational framework designed to map microscale traffic activity and relative emission landscapes by fusing multisource geospatial data and deep learning workflows. Focusing on the unmonitored context of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, our methodology uses very high resolution 15 cm satellite imagery to train and deploy a localised YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once, version 8) computer vision model, establishing an empirical baseline of fleet distribution. These static counts are dynamically distributed across the urban road network using a probabilistic Hub and Spoke Gravity Model, which is weighted through a zero shot Large Language Model semantic reclassification of unstructured OpenStreetMap features. Reconstructed kinematic flows are subsequently processed through velocity dependent Tier 3 EMEP/EEA algorithms to capture the nonlinear emission penalties triggered by severe network gridlock. To ensure framework defensibility, an independent unmanned aerial vehicle observation campaign was executed across ten distinct urban sites. The drone data directly validate model estimated physical parameters, achieving robust correlations for traffic volumes (R2 = 0.826) and link speeds (R2 = 0.925). Because literature derived chemical emission factors cannot be validated in situ, all absolute outputs are subjected to a rigorous multiparameter sensitivity analysis to report findings strictly as bounded ranges. The results reveal a clear structural handover in the spatial activity profile of the city. Daytime pollution is heavily driven by the informal paratransit fleet, which accounts for a bounded range of 82.8% to 95.1% of total PM2.5 emissions along primary corridors despite representing a numerical minority of active vehicles. Conversely, nocturnal baseline emissions transition to a landscape dominated almost entirely by private passenger vehicles. All code, processing pipelines, and validation datasets are available in a FAIR compliant open access repository. This framework establishes a scalable, remote sensing driven blueprint for diagnosing traffic activity structures in unmonitored metropolitan regions worldwide.

title: Integrating multi-source physical knowledge into deep learning for satellite soil moisture downscaling
abstract: Fine-resolution soil moisture (SM) is essential for understanding land–atmosphere interactions and managing hydrological hazards at local scales. Passive microwave remote sensing provides reliable SM observations but is limited by its coarse spatial resolution. Spatial downscaling offers an important means of addressing this limitation. However, many existing downscaling methods either rely on physical models with over-simplifications of soil hydrological knowledge, or data-driven models (particularly Deep Learning, DL) that lack interpretability, while current physics-guided DL approaches often emphasize a limited number of physical relationships or constraints. In response, this study proposes a framework to integrate multi-source physical knowledge into DL for satellite SM downscaling. Specifically, the framework incorporates physically informed drivers, a DisPATCh-informed physical regression branch, a hydrologically motivated consistency loss, and a constrained SM boundary loss, while using a gating module to adaptively fuse physically guided and data-driven representations. Evaluations based on in-situ and aircraft SM observations, together with coarse-scale consistency checks against SMAP SM, show that the proposed framework can effectively downscale SMAP SM from 9 km to 500 m. Using region-specific models across ten environmentally diverse regions, MPhy achieved station-averaged Pearson’s R and ubRMSE values of 0.76 and 0.05 m3/m3, respectively; the corresponding values for the pure-DL baseline Dens were 0.68 and 0.06 m3/m3. Detailed experiments in WGEW further showed that MPhy generally performed better than the pure-DL baseline, DisPATCh, single-physics-informed models, and selected conventional machine-learning methods. Overall, the results support improved physical plausibility and convergence efficiency, as well as framework robustness across the evaluated environments.

title: Adaptive smooth constrained stereo matching and disparity refinement for satellite DSM generation
abstract: High-resolution satellite images often exhibit substantial geometric and radiometric differences, making it difficult for conventional stereo matching methods to achieve high matching accuracy while suppressing noise and preserving object boundaries. To address this issue, this study improves both stereo matching and disparity post-processing in the satellite digital surface model (DSM) generation workflow. First, within the semi-global matching (SGM) framework, a mixed matching cost is constructed by combining the Census transform and gradient descriptors. Image gradients and edge cues extracted by a pretrained PiDiNet are then incorporated to adaptively control the strength of the smoothness constraint during cost aggregation, thereby improving matching reliability while balancing noise suppression and disparity-boundary preservation. Second, we propose a disparity post-processing method that combines improved weighted least-squares disparity refinement with matching-cost-based disparity fusion. The method first dynamically adjusts the smoothing weights to reduce texture-copying artifacts and edge blurring and then fuses disparity using matching costs to alleviate staircase artifacts caused by excessive smoothing. Experiments were conducted on ZY3-02 and WorldView-3 satellite imagery, with SGM, S2P-HD, Agisoft Metashape software, guided aggregation net, and FoundationStereo included for comparison. Across three test scenes dominated by urban and agricultural areas, the proposed method increased the proportion of pixels with absolute elevation errors below 2 m by an average of 4.12 percentage points and reduced RMSE by an average of 0.11 m compared with standard SGM. Qualitative results further show that the proposed method effectively suppresses noise in relatively flat regions while preserving building boundaries.

title: A large-scale spatiotemporal NDVI prediction method coupling multivariable constraints and structured modeling
abstract: Accurate prediction of vegetation dynamics is essential for understanding terrestrial ecosystems carbon and water cycles. However, existing Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) prediction methods are limited in their ability to represent spatiotemporal heterogeneity and nonlinear interactions among multiple driving variables, which restrict predictive accuracy and extrapolation performance at large scales. To address these limitations, this study proposed a structured large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction method incorporating multivariable constraints (MCS-LSTP) to characterize vegetation dynamics in complex and heterogeneous environments. MCS-LSTP incorporates multiple key driving variables and enhances the comprehensive representation of complex spatiotemporal dependencies and spatial heterogeneity through homogeneous spatial unit partitioning, unit-level temporal modeling, and continuous surface reconstruction. Results showed that MCS-LSTP model exhibited superior performance in terms of stability and prediction accuracy when compared to AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest (RF), and Transformer models. The mean Population Stability Index (PSI) reached 0.0572, with 98.7% of prediction units exhibiting PSI values below 0.1, indicating no significant deviation between the observed and simulated NDVI values. The average R2 and RMSE on the test set were 0.8551 and 0.2171, respectively. Furthermore, MCS-LSTP accurately reproduced seasonal NDVI fluctuations and meridional spatial gradients, with particularly high agreement between simulated and reference values during the growing season. This study provides a robust and scalable solution for large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction and offers critical technical support for ecological risk assessment in the Yellow River Basin and other ecologically vulnerable regions.

title: Hillslope-scale daily snow cover reconstruction in complex mountains: a novel framework integrating long-term snow persistence
abstract: Spatially continuous daily snow cover mapping at the hillslope scale (<100 m) is essential for resolving terrain-induced heterogeneity in hydrological processes and supporting mountain infrastructure management. Yet accurately characterizing daily snow cover heterogeneity at this scale remains challenging due to observational limitations and the difficulty of resolving terrain-controlled snow accumulation and ablation dynamics. To address this challenge, we developed a hillslope-scale daily snow cover reconstruction (HDSR) framework that explicitly incorporates long-term snow persistence as a structural spatial prior. The framework reconciles coarse-resolution daily Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) observations with a 30 m climatological snow cover frequency (SCOF) dataset, which characterizes terrain-mediated long-term snow persistence and constrains the spatial allocation of daily snow cover at the sub-pixel scale. HDSR is implemented through three sequential stages: spatiotemporal continuity restoration (STR), SCOF-constrained spatial refinement (SSR), and spatiotemporal snow-cover inference (SSI). A high-quality 30 m reference dataset was first constructed using the Snow Mapping Algorithm Considering Different Lighting Conditions (SALC), which was identified as the optimal approach through a systematic evaluation of seven candidate snow-mapping methods. The HDSR framework was subsequently applied to the Qilian Mountains and adjacent regions (QMAR), generating a daily 30 m binary snow cover product over an extensive mountainous region (536,018 km2) from September 2013 to August 2025. Validation against independent Landsat 8 observations yielded an F1-score (FS) of 0.873 and Cohen’s kappa (CK) of 0.859, while Bias values close to unity indicated negligible systematic bias in snow-cover representation. Consistent results obtained from independent Landsat 9 observations and time-lapse photography further supported the validity of the reconstruction, although site-specific evaluation revealed reduced capability for reconstructing short-lived snow events. The reconstructed dataset markedly outperforms the corresponding coarse-resolution baseline while providing enhanced spatial details. Compared with machine-learning models that exclude SCOF-related predictors, the proposed framework yields notable improvements, increasing FS and CK by 4.1% and 4.6%, respectively. Long-term snow persistence provides unique information unavailable from daily MODIS observations alone and is essential for resolving hillslope-scale snow heterogeneity. This study advances hillslope-scale daily snow cover mapping and potentially contributes to improved hydrological modeling and snow hazard assessment in complex mountainous environments.

title: SAMWater: a prompt-guided multimodal framework for transferable water mapping with the segment anything model
abstract: Accurate and transferable surface water mapping is critical for water resource assessment, flood monitoring, and aquatic ecosystem management, but remains difficult because SAR speckle, optical contamination, heterogeneous backgrounds, and scarce high-quality pixel-level annotations limit robust large-scale mapping. We propose SAMWater, a prompt-guided multimodal framework that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3). Instead of using SAR and optical data as independent classifiers, SAMWater transforms their complementary information into structured prompts for coarse-to-refined water segmentation. A physically interpretable multisensor coarse water prior is first generated from Sentinel observations using an automatic threshold-based strategy. This prior is then refined through prompt-based boundary refinement, a multi-prompt excavation strategy that derives point, box, and Gaussian-style mask prompts, and Water-IoU fine-tuning for water-specific candidate ranking. Using globally distributed samples and manually interpreted PlanetScope reference labels, SAMWater achieved average Kappa coefficients of 90.71%, 85.63%, and 89.05% in evaluations stratified by water body type, land cover background, and climatic zone, respectively. It generally outperformed traditional thresholding and clustering methods, public deep learning models, and existing global water or land cover products, particularly in structurally complex river, reservoir, urban, agricultural, and mountainous scenes. Ablation experiments confirmed that multimodal prior fusion, structured prompt construction, and water-specific ranking jointly drive the performance gains. Moreover, SAMWater-generated refined labels improved the training of U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer, indicating their utility for weakly supervised segmentation. SAMWater therefore demonstrates that integrating physically interpretable remote sensing priors with promptable foundation models provides a practical pathway for transferable surface water mapping, large-scale multisensor weak-label generation, and more consistent monitoring of surface water extent.

title: Tracking vegetation disturbance, recovery, and sustainability in open-pit mining areas of Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region from 2000 to 2024
abstract: Evaluating the overarching efficacy of mine greening initiatives and supporting land resource management within open-pit mining areas requires accurate long-term monitoring of both vegetative degradation and its subsequent regenerative phases. Overcoming the bottlenecks of conventional methods in decoupling vegetation abrupt disturbances from gradual recovery processes, this research utilizes the Google Earth Engine (GEE) and Landsat data spanning from 2000 to 2024. The investigation explicitly targets open-pit mining areas across the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. Through the synergistic integration of the Continuous Change Detection and Classification (CCDC) and an adaptively refined NDVImed,t segmentation baseline, we extracted the spatiotemporal dynamics of abrupt vegetation disturbance and gradual recovery events. Furthermore, to rigorously quantify the enduring stability and long-term persistence of these vegetation dynamic trajectories, the study coupled the non-parametric Sen–MK trend estimator with calculations of the Hurst exponent. The results demonstrate that the F1 score for detecting disturbance and recovery events over the past 25 years stably exceeded 0.8, exhibiting excellent temporal robustness. The derived chronological trajectories pinpoint 2013 as a significant turning point for vegetation dynamics. Before this critical juncture, the landscape suffered from intense degradation, marked by an average annual vegetative deficit of 962.19 ha. In the post-2013 era, a recovery-dominated paradigm emerged, characterized by an average yearly restoration of 831.37 ha. Crucially, the aggregate intensity of this vegetation greenness reached 1.64, substantially overshadowing the historical extraction-induced disturbance magnitude of 1.23. Concurrently, evaluations of trajectory persistence reveal that while a substantial 36.56% of the monitored landscape is undergoing sustained ecological enhancement, whereas 22.46% was characterized by persistent deterioration. Precipitation and temperature showed a limited influence on vegetation dynamics (R2 = 0.0796, p = 0.402), while enterprise consolidation and reclamation policies were the main drivers for post-2013 recovery. The acquired quantitative remote sensing evidence not only reveals the core role of macro-policy regulation in driving the reshaping of surface landscapes in mining areas but also provides solid scientific support for the future refined ecological governance of regional territorial space.

title: A review of remote sensing for agricultural drought: technologies, indices, modelling advances and future prospects
abstract: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on Remote Sensing (RS)-driven agricultural drought monitoring and prediction. Eligible studies were identified from the Web of Science and Scopus databases (last searched in August 2025); review articles, duplicates, and irrelevant studies were excluded, resulting in 181 articles. This review critically examined the evolution of sensors, drought indices, modelling approaches, and emerging technologies used to assess agricultural drought across diverse agro-ecological regions. Specifically, we (1) systematically evaluated the use of optical, thermal, and microwave RS platforms, along with satellite-based, model-based, and reanalysis products for agricultural drought monitoring; (2) reviewed widely used RS-based drought indices, including single indices grouped into nine categories, as well as composite indices; (3) reviewed software or programming languages applied; (4) assessed the progression of modelling approaches from traditional statistical and time-series methods to machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks; and (5) examined validation strategies applied to agricultural drought assessment. The analysis reveals a growing research interest in this topic, with a strong geographic concentration in Asia, particularly China. Optical and thermal platforms (e.g. MODIS and Landsat) dominate the literature (~54%) due to their accessibility, followed by satellite-derived precipitation products (17%), while microwave soil-moisture missions remain underutilized (~7%). Regarding RS-based indices, most studies employed more than one index: 44% analysed multiple individual indices, 51% used composite indices (either alone or in combination with individual indices), and only 5% relied on a single index. Vegetation indices, such as NDVI, remain workhorses; however, their sensitivity to soil background effects and canopy saturation has driven increased adoption of thermal composites (e.g. VHI), as well as adaptive weighting schemes and principal component analysis-based approaches. Moreover, computational tools used in drought research can be broadly grouped into geospatial and RS platforms for large-scale data processing and analysis (e.g. QGIS, GEE), and general-purpose programming languages (e.g. R, Python) for model development and advanced analytics. Regarding the methodology, statistical and time-series approaches account for 64% of the reviewed studies, followed by ML models (20%) and DL methods (15%), while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) remains nascent. Techniques, such as random forests, support vector machines, and CNN and LSTM architectures, generally outperform traditional models but require large training datasets and raise concerns related to interpretability and ethics. In terms of validation, hydro-climatic indices such as SPI and SPEI are most commonly used (32%), followed by crop yield and yield anomaly data (19%). This review further identifies key research gaps across sensors, indices, and modelling approaches and proposes a roadmap for developing equitable, interpretable, and resilient agricultural drought monitoring systems. Emerging opportunities include context-aware and interpretable AI, multi-sensor and multi-scale data fusion across optical, thermal, and microwave domains, integration of physiologically meaningful indicators such as sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), robust uncertainty quantification, and the development of hybrid and physics-informed modelling frameworks.

title: Beyond accuracy: environment-dependent performance and threshold robustness of spectral water indices across regions and seasons
abstract: Spectral water indices are widely used for operational surface-water mapping, yet large-scale automation is often hindered by threshold uncertainty and limited cross-scene transferability. Existing studies typically rank indices by peak accuracy while overlooking the critical trade-off between maximal performance and sensitivity to threshold perturbations. Here we establish a broad multi-region, multi-season benchmark using Sentinel-2 imagery, covering 12 environmentally heterogeneous regions and four seasons (48 scenes). Twelve representative indices are assessed in terms of scene-adaptive peak accuracy (F1max) and threshold robustness, quantified by a newly proposed Robustness Smoothness Index (RSI). We also introduce PCA-Bridge, which embeds scenes using environmental variables only and maps performance and robustness landscapes in the resulting environmental space. Rather than identifying a single universal index, our analysis reveals a clear trade-off between peak accuracy and threshold robustness. While a median F1max>0.92 across 48 scenes suggests generally high performance, performance declines markedly in complex environments, particularly those dominated by snow and ice. NDWI attains high peak accuracy (F1max≥0.95) in 50.0% of scenes but shows low robustness (RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 in only 8.3%), indicating strong threshold sensitivity. By comparison, MBWI and AWEInsh achieve the highest median F1max (0.968 and 0.960), whereas WI2015 and NWI exhibit the strongest robustness overall, with the nhighest mean RSI (0.840 and 0.837) and broad robustness coverage (RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 in 87.5% of scenes). These findings support task-oriented index selection rather than one-size-fits-all ranking. Out-of-scene transfer experiments showed that scene-wise optimal performance does not guarantee threshold generalisation. Overall, the proposed framework helps identify when peak accuracy, robustness, and transfer performance align or diverge, supporting more reliable large-scale surface-water monitoring.

title: PGD-Net: Prompt-Guided Hybrid Transformer Decoder for building extraction from remote sensing images
abstract: Accurate building extraction from remote sensing imagery is essential for urban planning, cadastral mapping, and geographic information updating. However, existing methods still struggle with semantic degradation during feature decoding, small-building detection, and accurate boundary delineation. To address these issues, we propose PGD-Net, which integrates feature-conditioned prompt guidance into the decoding process for building extraction. The proposed method introduces learnable internal feature prompts to compensate for degraded building semantics. These prompts are further integrated into a hybrid Transformer decoding framework to guide feature reconstruction. Furthermore, a two-level optimization strategy is adopted: TOAM enhances small-building feature responses at the feature level, while a lightweight morphological post-processing step is applied at the output level to refine predicted masks and alleviate boundary discontinuities. Experiments were conducted on three public benchmark datasets, including Massachusetts, WHU, and Inria, as well as the newly constructed Xiamen Building Dataset (XM). PGD-Net achieved IoU scores of 76.81%, 92.05%, and 84.18% on the Massachusetts, WHU, and Inria datasets, respectively. It also delivered the best performance on the XM dataset, which contains a large number of dense urban village buildings with severe occlusions and shadows. The results demonstrate that PGD-Net effectively improves extraction completeness, boundary accuracy, and small-building detection performance in complex urban environments. The code is available at https://github.com/dawnlight129/PGD-Net.

title: RSFF: a reconciliation-sparse fusion framework for semantic segmentation of rocky desertification land in multimodal time series
abstract: Accurate identification of rocky desertification land (RDL) is crucial for ecological environment monitoring and management in karst regions. However, RDL extraction is often hindered by land-cover confusion, seasonal variability, and the fragmented, small, and irregular spatial distribution, when existing methods insufficiently exploit multi-temporal multimodal information. To address this issue, we construct the first dual-modal RDL semantic segmentation dataset with time series (RD dataset) and propose a reconciliation-sparse fusion framework (RSFF) for multi-temporal multimodal data. The framework adopts a dual-branch encoding architecture with multilevel spatio-temporal interaction to separately extract spatial and temporal features from optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imageries. Through the designed Convolutional Attention Reconciliation Module (CARM), multidimensional enhanced features are reconciled, and the Sparse Cross Fusion Module (SCFM) is employed to improve feature discriminability while reducing computational complexity compared with conventional dense attention mechanisms, enabling deep complementarity of cross-modal information. Experimental results on the RD dataset demonstrate that RSFF can effectively distinguish RDL from similar land-cover types, such as bare land and cropland, and significantly enhance RDL boundary delineation while maintaining high classification consistency. The mean intersection over union (mIoU) and overall accuracy (OA) reach 82.94% and 94.28%, respectively, outperforming other state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. In addition, experiments on the public PASTIS-R dataset further verify the robustness of RSFF under different landscape characteristics and small, fragmented parcel distributions. The RD dataset and code are available at https://github.com/laopiao-lp/RSFF.

title: Point-Cloud-Native L-Band Augmentation of SWOT KaRIn: Recovering Canopy-Shadowed Dark Water with NISAR
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: The SWOT mission's Ka-band Radar Interferometer (KaRIn) delivers surface-water observations at 15-25 m resolution but the operational Level-2 Pixel Cloud is known to miss pixels where dense canopy attenuates the specular return, flagging them as dark water. We show that co-registering NISAR L-band geocoded backscatter onto SWOT PIXC recovers dark-water pixels at matched precision. Over the Congo cuvette the augmentation lifts dark-water recall by 11.3 pp; over the Amazon varzea by 17.9 pp. Both gains clear a pre-registered 10 pp kill gate with disjoint 95% bootstrap confidence intervals versus baseline. A joint-shuffle falsifier confirms the gain is from real sensor information, not regularisation. To our knowledge this is the first combined use of NISAR and SWOT reported quantitatively.

title: Dual Retrieval Queries Fine-Tuning for Composed Image Retrieval
abstract: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) is a popular multi-modal retrieval task that aims to retrieve a target image based on a query composed of a reference image and modification text. The challenge lies in how to effectively retrieve a target image that preserves the visual content of the reference image while incorporating the changes described by the modification text. Existing CIR methods primarily employ a fusion-based strategy or a textual-inversion strategy during training. Although these methods have achieved promising results, they are limited in fully leveraging multi-modal information. This results in modality redundancy, where the retrieval process is dominated by one modality while ignoring the other. To address this issue, we propose an asymmetric fusion mechanism to generate dual retrieval queries of different granularity, enabling the model to fully use multi-modal information.
